title: Guard spec v1 — evidence file
description: One run's findings, on disk, in a shape an auditor can read without the tool. Each record binds a claim to a subject (for TestGuard, an injected fault) and a verdict, with every run that produced the verdict.

snapshot.description: When the working tree was probed instead of `head`: the dangling commit that captured it. Not a ref; may be garbage-collected.

ignoredDirty.description: Defender/target files that had uncommitted changes when `head` was probed as committed (an explicit --ref, or --ignore-dirty). The working-tree versions of these files are NOT what the verdicts describe.

source.description: `project`: the runner package resolved from the project and its own bin script ran. `path`: no such package in the project; an executable of that name on PATH ran instead (a legitimate monorepo setup, but not the project's pinned version).

confirmRuns.description: N — how many times the defenders were run both unmodified (baseline) and with each fault applied.

provisional.description: True iff confirmRuns < 3. A provisional run's verdicts are not confirmed: they must not be frozen into a baseline and must be rendered as provisional wherever they appear. Validators enforce the equivalence in both directions.

mode.description: `worktree` = faults were applied in a scratch git worktree (default). `in-place` = the user's working tree was mutated and restored.

outcome.description: `fail` means at least one test failed with the suite otherwise loading and running. `error` means the suite could not load or run (import/syntax error). `timeout` means the runner exceeded its budget.

assertionFailures.description: Test-level failures that are neither timeouts nor load failures: the test body ran and rejected the behaviour, whether by an assertion or by an exception the fault caused. Only these count toward `killed`. A timeout or a suite that fails to load is not evidence that the suite defends the claim.

fingerprint.description:
sha256 of `<claim.id>
<subject.id>
<subject.file>
<verdict>`. Derived from identities and outcome, never from `find`/`replace`, so repairing a rotted anchor does not churn the baseline.

subject.description: What was tried against the claim. For TestGuard `kind` is `fault`. Other adopters use their own kinds (e.g. `doc-statement`, `finding`); extra properties are permitted here and nowhere else.

contentHash.description: sha256 of the subject's content (for a fault: find + newline + replace). Excluded from the fingerprint on purpose, so repairing an anchor does not churn a baseline — and recorded here on purpose, so weakening a fault to make a finding disappear is visible.

baselineRuns.description: Defenders run on unmodified source, N times. Anything short of N/N pass is `flaky-defender`.

probeRuns.description: Defenders run with the fault applied, N times.

escalated.description: True when the fault survived its declared defenders and a broader test set was then run.

undeclaredKillers.description: With reason `killed-by-undeclared-tests`: the tests (as `file::name`) that failed in every escalation run. Names what to add to `defendedBy`.

anchor.description: With an anchor-related reason: how many times `find` occurred versus how many were expected.

discovered.description: True when no defenders were declared and `resolved` was found by static import of the subject's file.

inputs.description: Content hashes of everything the verdict depends on, so an unchanged claim can reuse its prior verdict.

reusedFrom.description: Run id whose verdict was reused because `inputs` were unchanged.

blastRadius.description: Number of source files that import the subject's file, transitively or directly as the tool documents.
